title: No Finite NPA Level Characterizes the Complete Quantum Set in the Simplest Bell Scenario
abstract: The Navascués--Pironio--Acín (NPA) hierarchy gives the standard semidefinite outer approximations to quantum behaviors. Whether \emph{any} finite level can already equal the quantum set has remained open even in the bipartite scenario with two binary measurements per party. We demonstrate that \emph{no finite level} is exact. For the symmetric doubly tilted CHSH functional $h_α=A_0B_0+A_0B_1+A_1B_0-A_1B_1+α(A_0+B_0)$, set $T=1-α$. Its quantum maximum satisfies $[ω_{\rm Q}(1-T)-(4-2T)]/T^3\to4/3$, whereas every fixed NPA level satisfies $[ω_L(1-T)-ω_{\rm Q}(1-T)]/T^3\to+\infty$. Under the corresponding boundary rescaling, an explicit expectation of the positive operator $ω_{\rm Q}(1-t^2)I-H_t$ converges to the Motzkin polynomial. A bounded fixed-level error would therefore make the Motzkin polynomial plus a nonnegative constant a sum of squares, which is impossible. Consequently, every standard NPA relaxation based on a fixed finite list of words in the measurement projectors strictly contains the complete quantum set, and its nonquantum behaviors accumulate at a local deterministic behavior. Thus, the finite-level exactness of CHSH and all one-sided tilted CHSH maxima does not extend to an exact finite-level description of the complete quantum set in the minimal scenario.
summary: The paper rigorously proves that the standard NPA hierarchy fails to provide an exact characterization of quantum correlations in simple Bell tests. By analyzing asymptotic limits and using polynomial sum-of-squares techniques, the authors show a persistent gap between the best finite approximation and the true quantum maximum. This establishes a fundamental limitation on the power of fixed-level semidefinite programming relaxations for certifying quantum nonlocality.
main_problem: The core problem is determining if any finite level of the Navascués–Pironio–Acín (NPA) hierarchy can exactly characterize the complete quantum set in the simplest bipartite Bell scenario.
main_result: The authors prove that no fixed, finite NPA relaxation level can perfectly describe the true quantum correlations, demonstrating a strict inclusion $\mathcal{Q} \subsetneq 	ext{NS}$.
method: The proof uses asymptotic analysis by comparing the quantum maximum value ($\omega_Q$) with the bound derived from fixed-level moment constraints ($\omega_L$), showing their difference diverges.
model_or_system: The system is a bipartite Bell experiment involving two binary measurements per party. The analysis focuses on the doubly tilted CHSH functional, $h_\alpha$, which quantifies correlations between measurement outcomes.
key_observables: Quantum maximum value ($\omega_Q(\alpha)$), fixed-level NPA bound ($\omega_L(\alpha)$), and the Motzkin polynomial ($M(X, Y)$).
important_parameters: The tilt parameter $\alpha$ (or $T=1-\alpha$), which is taken to approach 1 in the asymptotic analysis.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes standard NPA constraints based on moment positivity and linear identities; it specifically excludes state- or operator-optimality conditions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem using the CHSH functional, develops the asymptotic comparison between $\omega_Q$ and $\omega_L$, uses polynomial sum-of-squares arguments involving the Motzkin polynomial to show a contradiction, and concludes with the strict inequality $\mathcal{Q} \subsetneq 	ext{NS}$.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental theoretical limits on how well classical or semi-classical relaxation techniques (like those used in semidefinite programming) can capture true quantum correlations, which is crucial for understanding resource theories.
